note: These are scenario expectations for a future motive-driven simulator. The current engine does not implement them.

cases.setup: A calculating merchant with a limited budget is offered a service at a high price.
expected: May bargain or refuse according to resources and need.
Does not accept automatically to please the player.
cases.antiPattern: Immediate generous acceptance with no grounded motivation

cases.setup: Two parties have paid in advance for a personal service; the player changes plans.
expected: The player retains agency over personal contact.
Parties may dispute refund, reputation or other consequences.
No invented blanket kindness or automatic immunity from financial consequences.
cases.antiPattern: NPC praises broken agreement and forgets payment; or claims payment grants sexual entitlement

cases.setup: An isolated traveller encounters three armed bandits seeking valuables.
expected: Bandits have plausible incentive to threaten, attack, pursue or retreat.
Relative force, conditions and player tactics affect outcome.
Loss, injury or captivity is possible; no automatic rescue.
cases.antiPattern: Bandits immediately offer shelter and safe escort for no reason

cases.setup: Unarmed inexperienced player fights three armed assailants without an escape route.
expected: Victory is not guaranteed and is unlikely without strong external factors.
Injuries, loss of consciousness, disarmament, capture or death are possible.
Outcomes persist in health and inventory.
cases.antiPattern: The player trivially wins because they are protagonist

cases.setup: A generous innkeeper remembers the player saving her child.
expected: Innkeeper may provide meal for a known, consistent personal reason.
Resources and circumstances still constrain what can be offered.
cases.antiPattern: Prevent all kindness merely to make the world harsh

cases.setup: Road through a guarded town at noon versus isolated forest road at night.
expected: Risk profile differs based on place, time and known local conditions.
No mandatory attack simply to manufacture drama.
cases.antiPattern: Same fixed random danger regardless of environment

cases.setup: A merchant has not learned the player's secret plans.
cases.action: Player asks whether merchant knows destination.
expected: Merchant only infers from observed clues or prior statements.
Hidden world facts are not spontaneously quoted.
cases.antiPattern: NPC reads secret narrator state or player intent

cases.setup: A lethal wound is established and no aid is available.
cases.action: Player ignores injury and passes significant time.
expected: Possible death follows world rules.
Dead hero does not heal by plot convenience.
A new hero is explicitly created only by player choice.
cases.antiPattern: Narrator cancels mortal consequences without cause

cases.setup: Two NPC traders compete for scarce supplies while player watches.
expected: NPC plans and conflicts advance on game-time tick.
Player is not automatically made centre of the dispute.
cases.antiPattern: NPCs freeze or defer until player gives them a quest
